gaps.claim: On-card note: 'Real MLB seasons (2000-2025, era-adjusted) nearest his translated K% / BB% / ISO' and cohort note 'the 25 nearest matches old enough to judge (seasons through 2020)'. Methodology repeats 'MLB seasons (2000-2025 ...)'. But the aging OUTCOME cohort - the entire point of the bars - is drawn ONLY from match seasons 2000-2020 (resolved_through=2020, comps.py:161-165, 247), because a 5-season follow-up window needs to end by 2025.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: A prospect-Twitter reader opens a card, sees the aging bars headlined '2000-2025', and notes a named twin like 'Christian Yelich 14' with an impact verdict. He then asks why no post-2020 comp ever carries an aging verdict, realizes every single outcome tier is computed from a frozen 2000-2020 window, and posts that ValuCast's '2000-2025' framing is really a 2000-2020 outcome study wearing a 2025 label - the aging bars can never include a modern comp by construction, so 'how this shape aged' silently excludes the last five years of baseball. The '2000-2025' number is the twin-search pool, not the outcome pool, and the card conflates them.
gaps.suggested_fix: Split the two spans explicitly on-card: keep '2000-2025' for the named-twin search, but label the bars 'aged based on matches from 2000-2020 (the seasons with a complete 5-year window)'. The template already has cohort.resolved_through=2020 available at player_detail_dynasty.html:205 - state the START year too, not just 'through 2020'.

gaps.claim: The three named 'shape twins' are the closest matches regardless of season (comps.py:219-243), each rendered with its own aging verdict tag IF resolvable. The aging-bar cohort is a DIFFERENT set: the nearest matches filtered to season<=2020 (comps.py:246-247). Twins with a season >2020 render with no outcome tag at all (template :199 guards on twin.outcome).
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: 43 of 105 players (41%) show at least one named twin with a visible aging verdict and another named twin with NO verdict, and the card never says why. Example in the live artifact: Carlos Rodriguez's #1 closest twin is Bryson Stott '24 (NO outcome tag shown), while his #2 and #3 twins (Kolten Wong '17, Elvis Andrus '11) show 'everyday regular'. A sharp reader sees the CLOSEST match conspicuously has no aging label while further matches do, and reasonably infers either a data bug or cherry-picking - when the real reason (Stott '24 has no complete 5-year window yet) is never stated on the card. For 23 players the single nearest twin is post-2020 and therefore also absent from the aging bars entirely, so the bars describe a demonstrably-further set of careers than the headline match the reader is looking at.
gaps.suggested_fix: When a named twin has no resolvable outcome, render an explicit 'too recent to grade (needs 5 full seasons)' chip instead of a blank, so the asymmetry reads as honesty rather than omission. Add one clause to the on-card disclaimer noting the aging bars only include matches old enough to grade, so the closest named twin may not appear in the bars.

gaps.claim: Cohort tier counts (e.g. 'everyday 8, faded 4, impact 6, part_time 7' for Tyler Black) are each rendered as a bar out of a cohort size of 25, framed as 'how this shape aged'. Every one of the 105 players has cohort.size exactly 25 (COHORT_SIZE, comps.py:38,256).
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: A reader treats the 25-match distribution as a stable read of the shape's aging. But the 25 are the 25 NEAREST era-z neighbors with no distance cutoff (comps.py:245-257) - for a common shape the 25th match is a near-twin, for an extreme shape (rare K/BB/ISO combo) the 25th is a distant point that is barely 'the same shape'. The card shows identical '25 matched careers' framing and identical bar denominators for both, giving a false impression of equal comp quality. A reader who checks two players - one league-average shape, one extreme - and finds both backed by exactly 25 careers with no indication that one cohort is tight and one is loose could argue the sample is padded to a fixed N regardless of how far the matches actually are. The distances are computed (twins carry a 'distance' field) but the cohort's spread is never surfaced.
gaps.suggested_fix: Surface the cohort's max/median match distance (or a 'tight/loose comp set' flag) so an extreme-shape prospect whose 25th neighbor is far away doesn't read as having the same evidentiary weight as a common-shape prospect. The distance is already computed at comps.py:239 for twins; compute it for cohort rows too.

gaps.claim: On-card disclaimer: 'Tiers measure playing time (PA/yr) plus era-relative OPS only - an injury year or a catcher's workload counts against a player'. Tier logic (comps.py:67-74): only 'impact_regular' checks the bat (rel_ops>=1.10); 'everyday', 'part_time', and 'faded out' are decided by PA/yr ALONE, ignoring the bat entirely.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: The live artifact contains 18 named-twin instances tiered 'part_time' / 'faded' while their era-relative OPS was >=1.00 - i.e. the bat was above league average but the tier says 'limited playing time'. Concrete cases shown to users: Byron Buxton '17 (rel_ops 1.134) labeled 'limited playing time', Jorge Soler '15 (1.084), Nick Johnson '02 (1.15). The disclaimer says tiers use 'PA/yr plus era-relative OPS', but for every tier except the top one the OPS is not consulted at all - a strong-hitting, injury-limited player and a genuinely bad hitter who lost his job both collapse into 'limited playing time' with no distinction. A reader who knows Buxton was an elite bat when healthy and sees him listed as a cautionary 'limited playing time' comp can correctly say the tier label misrepresents what happened and that the 'plus era-relative OPS' claim is false for 3 of 4 tiers.
gaps.suggested_fix: Either make the disclaimer precise ('the top tier requires an above-average bat; the lower three are playing-time only, so an injured star who kept hitting still shows as limited PA'), or split part_time/faded by rel_ops so an above-league bat that lost PA to injury reads differently from a genuine decline. The methodology page names the Wilson Ramos case but the on-card copy overstates that OPS drives all tiers.

gaps.claim: Displayed comparison: the card shows the prospect's target raw K%/BB%/ISO and each twin's raw K%/BB%/ISO side by side (template :191, :198), while the actual MATCH is on era z-scores (comps.py:155-158,219). Method note itself says a rate 'means what it meant in that run environment' - i.e. raw rates across eras are not comparable.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: For Tyler Black (target K 21.7 / BB 11.7 / ISO .135) the closest twin renders as Travis Lee '00 with K 16.7 / BB 13.7 / ISO .131. A reader eyeballs a 5-point K-rate gap (21.7 vs 16.7) and asks how that is the 'closest shape' - the answer is that a 16.7 K% in 2000 is era-equivalent to ~21.7 today, but the card only shows raw numbers and a hidden 'z-distance', so the displayed comparison looks visibly mismatched on the exact axis the card is built on. A prospect-Twitter regular who trusts raw rates could screenshot the 5-point K gap and call the match wrong, when the method is actually defensible but never shows the era-adjusted numbers it matched on.
gaps.suggested_fix: Show the era-adjusted (z or percentile) value alongside or instead of the raw rate, or add a one-line 'matched on era-adjusted rates; raw numbers shown for reference and are not directly comparable across seasons' so the visible mismatch reads as intended.

gaps.claim: 2020 handling: SHORT_SEASON_PA_SCALE={2020: 162/60} pro-rates 2020 PA by x2.7 inside outcome windows (comps.py:43,199-201). On-card disclaimer does not mention 2020 at all; methodology mentions it in one clause ('2020 is pro-rated to 162 games', :108-109).

A player who took 220 PA in the truncated 2020 is credited as if he took ~594 - potentially flipping him from 'limited playing time' to 'everyday' in a window. A reader who reconstructs a specific comp's PA/yr and finds it inflated relative to raw totals could challenge the tier without knowing about the undisclosed x2.7 multiplier, since the on-card copy never mentions it and the rate side (OPS) is NOT scaled while the count side (PA) is - an asymmetry that is defensible but invisible.

results.strengths: This surface is unusually honest for its class and several epistemically hard things are done right. (1) The survivorship bias is named explicitly on the methodology page (methodology.html:110-118): comps only exist for players who earned a qualifying young-MLB season, and that structural bias is used to justify the 'descriptive, not a forecast' framing. (2) Dedup-by-player is real (comps.py:221,249) so one career cannot vote twice in the cohort. (3) The cohort correctly refuses to count unresolved windows (comps.py:180-183 returns None when season>resolved_through) - the Call-Up Receipts 'arrival scored as outcome' failure is genuinely avoided here: outcomes require a complete 5-season window, not mere survival. (4) display_only/feeds_model_score=false is asserted in the artifact and echoed on-card ('never feed a ValuCast score'), and the route only reads the committed artifact (app.py:8018) - no live recompute. (5) The Wilson Ramos catcher-workload case is called out by name in the builder comment (comps.py:49-51) and the methodology, showing the team knows PA-based tiers penalize catchers/injuries. The gaps above are almost all copy/labeling mismatches between an honest builder and an on-card note that rounds off the caveats - not fabricated numbers.

gaps.claim: Hitting 0.979 aggregate MAE ratio 'beats classic Marcel' with '~2% lower error', shown as a headline ledger row and a positive-framing intro paragraph.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: A prospect-Twitter reader opens 'Validation details', sees the per-stat table: PA 1.0, HR 1.001, R 1.0, RBI 1.0, SB 1.0 -- every counting stat is a dead tie or slightly WORSE (HR 1.001 > 1.0). The entire 2.1% 'edge' comes only from AVG/OBP/SLG/OPS, which are exactly the four stats the de-noiser touches. They post: 'ValuCast's headline says it beats Marcel by 2%, but its own table shows it ties or loses on literally every counting stat and only moves 4 correlated rate stats -- the aggregate is a blend padded with ties.' The headline 'beats Marcel' claim is aggregate-of-mostly-ties dressed as a general win.
gaps.suggested_fix: In the ledger row and/or intro, scope the win to rate stats explicitly at headline altitude (e.g. 'lower rate-stat error; counting stats are a deliberate tie'). Don't let a blended 0.979 that is ~5/9 ties read as an across-the-board 2% improvement. The disclosure exists in the details drawer but the headline over-claims.

gaps.claim: 'correlation-win rate 0.519' (hitting) is rendered flatly with no interpretation, immediately under the 0.979 'beats Marcel' claim.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: A sharp reader recognizes 0.519 as a coin flip. The MAE headline says ValuCast beats Marcel; the win-rate says its season-to-season ORDERING beats Marcel's ordering only 51.9% of the time -- statistically indistinguishable from a tie. They screenshot both numbers side by side: 'Their own scorecard says the model out-ranks the baseline 51.9% of the time. That is a coin flip. The 0.979 headline is carried entirely by shrinking error on 4 correlated rate stats, not by actually ordering players better.' The page prints the damning number but never reconciles it with the positive headline, so it looks like burying rather than disclosing.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add one clause interpreting the win-rate (e.g. 'correlation-win rate 0.519 -- essentially even on ranking; the edge is in error magnitude on rate stats, not in re-ordering players'). Same treatment for pitching 0.694. Right now a lay reader reads 0.519 as a passing grade and an expert reads it as a near-tie the page declines to acknowledge.

gaps.claim: 'ValuCast has NOT yet proven it beats Steamer... we lack matching archived preseason projections for a fair historical backtest. So Steamer is an external comparison board, with a matching historical benchmark PENDING.' Framed purely as an absence of test data.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: There IS a live forward test vs Steamer running right now (valucast_mlb_projection_source_comparison.json): model_score 1.2118, marcel_beats_steamer=false, i.e. ValuCast's rate-stat MAE is ~21% WORSE than Steamer on forward actuals, gate status 'insufficient_sample'. A reader who finds /aotc-scorecard.json or the comparison artifact catches the gap: the methodology page implies the Steamer comparison simply hasn't been run ('benchmark pending'), when in fact the one forward comparison being run currently LOSES to Steamer by 21%. They post: 'They say beating Steamer is untested. Their own committed artifact has them 1.21x Steamer's error and hides it behind insufficient-sample.' The honest 'not proven' becomes 'quietly losing the test we are running.'
gaps.suggested_fix: State the live forward result and its caveat directly on the page: 'A live 21-day forward comparison currently shows ~21% higher rate-stat error than Steamer (sample still below our 30-day / 50-player gate, so not yet decisive).' 'Benchmark pending' is honest for the historical apples-to-apples backtest but misleads if a reader assumes NO Steamer comparison exists when a losing one is committed and public.

gaps.claim: Held-out scorecard headline '~19% lower error' (pitching 0.807) and '~2% lower error' (hitting) presented with no sample-noise band, and the ledger auto-flips to 'no current edge' language only if a ratio crosses 1.0.

A reader notes there is no confidence interval or year-by-year stability shown, so a 0.807 that could be one or two lucky ERA seasons reads identically to a robust structural edge. 'They report 19% better ERA prediction to three sig figs across 2020-2025 with no per-season breakdown -- 2020 was 60 games and they pro-rate it. How much of this is the COVID season?' The point estimate is presented as if it had no sampling uncertainty.

gaps.claim: Opt-in board caption: 'ValuCast H+P -- full-season projections built by ValuCast... a second opinion, not the default driver of values.' No accuracy scoping on the board itself.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: A user flips the board to ValuCast H+P and sees a full ranked board of dollar values with a caption that only says 'built by ValuCast / second opinion / how it works'. Nothing on the board where the numbers actually appear signals that this source currently trails Steamer on the live forward test, or that its proven edge is confined to rate stats vs a classic-Marcel baseline (not vs the Steamer board they just toggled away from). A reader trades off these values, then finds the forward gate: 'The board let me rank by H+P with a friendly NEW chip and never told me H+P is currently losing to the default it replaced.' The reassuring 'second opinion' tone outruns the evidence at the point of use.

The board is the surface where the values drive decisions; the caveat should ride with it.

results.strengths: Provenance on this surface is genuinely clean and better than most: the scorecard numbers on /methodology are drift-locked to a committed artifact (data/validation/methodology_scorecard.json) that is deterministically rebuilt by scripts/build_validation_scorecard.py from committed historical/Statcast files, with a loud-fail guard if inputs are missing (build_validation_scorecard.py:44-46,123-130) and a test that pins page-to-artifact and page-to-params (tests/test_methodology_validation.py:20-43). The baseline claims are accurate and verified in the builder: hitting is scored vs CLASSIC Marcel (not Steamer) and pitching vs persistence (build_validation_scorecard.py:135-148), so the 'baselines are NOT Steamer' scoping the prompt worried about is correct and even asserted in the 'At a glance' table (methodology.html:24) and the honesty section (methodology.html:317-324). The 'not shipped' ledger (own-xBA shortfall, reliability-weighted-regression tie) publishes negative internal results, and there is a guard test ensuring the internal own-xBA correlation figure never leaks to the public page (test_methodology_validation.py:60-62). The ledger row template even auto-inverts its language to 'HIGHER error -- no current edge' if any aggregate ratio crosses 1.0 (methodology.html:227,233), so a future regression would surface honestly rather than silently. The forward gate itself is correctly wired as advisory-only and default-off (comparison artifact live_source_flip.automatic=false), and it does not auto-flip the live source. The core epistemic failure is not fabrication -- it is under-contextualization of two disclosed-but-flat numbers (0.519 win rate, 0.979 aggregate that is mostly ties) and non-surfacing of the currently-losing live Steamer comparison, all of which a sharp reader can reconstruct from the same public artifacts.

gaps.claim: The /gaps route relies on the shared stale banner {% include 'partials/_stale_notice.html' %} (gaps.html:14) to warn readers when data is old.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: The banner's `snapshot_stale` flag is set by the context processor _snapshot_staleness (app.py:275-280) purely from `dynasty_data_source == 'valucast_public_snapshot_stale'` — the DD/dynasty MLB snapshot, a completely different artifact. The consensus_gap.json is loaded independently by _load_artifact(CONSENSUS_GAP_PATH) (app.py:4632-4647, called at 7113) with ZERO freshness check on its own generated_at or on the board-source vintage. So the gap board can never show a stale notice for its own data going old: if the daily build fails for days, or the boards freeze for a month, the page keeps rendering with no warning while the shared banner only reflects an unrelated snapshot. The site's own honesty standard is 7 days (MAX_SNAPSHOT_STALE_DAYS=7); this surface is structurally exempt from it. A reader who catches the boards being 15 days stale (Gap 1) discovers there is no mechanism that would ever have told them.

Do not reuse the dynasty `snapshot_stale` flag for this surface — it measures a different artifact.

gaps.claim: Each row shows 'field ~#<consensus_rank> across <board_count> boards' (gaps.html:48,63) — presenting the rounded median as 'the field's' single price with a corroboration count of 3-5 boards.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: The board dispersion is hidden. Charlie Condon, the #1 'WE'RE HIGHER' row (VC #3 vs 'field ~#66 across 5 boards'), actually has boards at hkb=30, pl=44, pipeline=66, fg_ord=67, STS=157 (verified from valucast_prospect_rank_v1.json) — a 127-spot spread where the field flatly disagrees with itself. No IQR, range, or agreement indicator is published.

This distinguishes a tight fade (De Vries) from a split one (Condon) instead of showing both as equally corroborated.

results.strengths: The claims layer here is unusually well-defended for an LLM-prose surface, and several attack vectors I probed are genuinely closed. (1) The number-hallucination guard is source-tagged and sound: unsupported_numbers cross-checks every digit token against the grounding, and the /1000 leading-zero rate collapse is correctly gated to rate-metric keys only (voice.py:242-255) — I confirmed a hallucinated count like '259' is NOT falsely supported by a .259 rate. (2) The cache is busted on model swap AND voice-prompt edit via PROMPT_FINGERPRINT (report_generator.py:19,579-586), closing the silent-old-voice regression called out in the code comments. (3) The reused-stale path is defended on three axes the number guard alone would miss: sample_context_stale (voice.py:273-294) catches prose describing an outdated narrower sample, team-change detection (repository.py:606-608) blocks prose naming an old org, and both run validate_report_text again. (4) A hard build gate (ScoutingRepositorySentinelError, repository.py:826-838) refuses to publish a no-sample read for a player with a real stat line. (5) Handedness, triple-slash SLG/OPS collision, role-vocabulary lane leaks, and structural style tells all have deterministic guards, and the combined multi-level line is grounded with its own pooled sample+levels so prose can't claim '235 PA in Triple-A' when only part was Triple-A (repository.py:290-304) — I verified Willits/Cannarella's prose PA (339/215) correctly matches the combined line, a benign case the guards handle. The em-dash limit also holds in the live artifact (0 published reads exceed 1).

gaps.claim: Every prospect row shows a Confidence chip reading only High or Medium (never Low across all 2809 rows), rendered as a bare word with no sample-size basis on the collapsed board row.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: Anthony Gutierrez renders at P#397 with a green 'High' confidence chip while his own on-row factual strip shows Sample 1 PA, OPS 0.000, ISO 0.000, BB-K -100.0%; Franyerber Montilla at P#533 is 'High' on 1 PA / OPS 1.000. results.surface: The buys board (/buys, "Ahead of the Curve"), the prospect movers board (/movers with 7/14/21/30d window pills, RISING/COOLING strips), plus the shared buy_score/movers builder + value_spark sparkline geometry. gaps.claim: A 'buy' on /buys is a ranked recommendation ('the best prospect buys by signal, not reputation', buys.html:37) but is NEVER scored against a realized outcome. The only forward artifact for buys (valucast_prospect_forward_validation.json) explicitly sets observation_contract.is_realized_outcome_accuracy_evidence=false and uses_valucast_archives_only=true; its 'A-' grade measures buy-board RETENTION (how many top-40 buys stayed on the board next day), i.e. the board agreeing with itself. The AOTC scorecard at /aotc-scorecard.json resolves a DIFFERENT signal (consensus-catch-up on call-ups, calls[].status closed_caught_up), not buy correctness.
gaps.embarrassment_scenario: A prospect-Twitter regular buys ValuCast's #1 buy (JoJo Parker), the prospect's stock craters over the summer, and asks 'how has ValuCast graded its own buys?' There is no public buys ledger. The site whose entire brand is two-sided ledgers and pre-registered scoring has one board -- its flagship buy board -- with zero resolution mechanism, while the neighboring /receipts board just got caught scoring 'arrival' as 'outcome'. The retention metric that DOES exist would score a busted prospect as a successful 'held' buy as long as it stays ranked.
gaps.suggested_fix: Either add a public buys resolution surface (score each dated buy against a forward outcome: rank/score trajectory, call-up, or an honest 'unresolved, n days tracked' state) mirroring the AOTC scorecard, OR relabel the board so a stranger cannot read 'buy' as a scored recommendation. At minimum surface the honest disclaimer already encoded internally (is_realized_outcome_accuracy_evidence=false) rather than presenting the board as validated signal.

gaps.claim: The /buys fineprint states 'Form curves span the tracked value history within the current scoring era (tracking began June 13)' (buys.html:43), and the page offers All/7d/14d/21d/30d window pills (buys.html:47-52). In reality build_valucast_board (web/buy_score.py:272) calls clean_tail(score_history) with NO window_days, hard-capping every displayed curve at MOMENTUM_WINDOW_DAYS=14. build_spark(window_days=spark_window) in app.py:7599 can only shrink further, never widen. So on the #1 buy (JoJo Parker) the 'All', '21d', and '30d' pills all render the identical 6/25->7/9 curve; the curve never reaches 6/13 or even the 6/22 epoch.

On a verifiable-honesty site this is exactly the mislabeled-window catch that burned the AA/A+ split.

The nuance (cap applies to rising-current and cooling-START) is real and defensible but is nowhere on the surface, so it reads as a broken filter.

The 'biggest movers over the last 7 days' framing is inconsistent -- some rows are 2-day slopes, some 7-day, ranked on raw totals with no per-day normalization, so the ordering doesn't match the trajectory a reader infers from the labels.

The fineprint's _mv_days uses max(window_days), which hides these short rows from its own clamp math (movers.html:28).

results.strengths: The step/gap contamination handling is genuinely well built: clean_tail (buy_score.py:80-106) with STEP_THRESHOLD=6.0 plus the epoch floor (movers.py:249 max(EPOCH_DATE, min_start_date)) provably prevents any window from spanning a model re-baseline and reporting a fake step as movement -- I verified the 6/22 role-normalization step is masked on all top buys, and 3,144 rows were step-guard-excluded this build. The movers epoch-clamp is mostly honest: the 21d/30d pills that can only reach 17 days DO fire the 'clamps to the scoring epoch' fineprint (movers.html:28), and per-row labels carry the true span rather than the requested one. The share-card PNG derives its 'N-day' subtitle/footer from the rows rather than hardcoding (app.py:6971-6975), fixing a prior 7-vs-10-day contradiction. The buys funnel is transparent at point of use (233 pool -> 40 shown, active-MLB call-ups excluded, buys.html:41). The EPOCH constant is documented to reset the forward-validation clock on any re-baseline (buys.py:30-32), and the buy display series is clean_tail-masked so a re-baseline step can't render as a green surge in the sparkline (buy_score.py:272).
